assignment: CSE 60745 (Fall 2026) HW3-Part(A): GNNs Hands-on Practice -- 30 points, Q1-Q5 at 6 points each

source_documents.questions: input/CSE 60745_Fall 2026_HW3-Part(A).docx (3 rendered pages; p1 cover, p2 preamble+Q1, p3 Q2-Q5)

problems.title: Q1 GCN, Q2 GAT, Q3 GIN, Q5 deep 8-hop layer (LastFM-Asia social graph)
subparts: Q1 (6 pts): complete MyGCNConv -- __init__, reset_parameters, forward, message; symmetric-normalised GCN with self-loops
Q2 (6 pts): complete MyGATConv in multi-head fashion, using torch_geometric.utils.softmax
Q3 (6 pts): complete MyGINConv -- sum aggregation, (1+eps) self term, own MLP, eps initialised to 0
Q5 (6 pts): complete MyDeepConv -- an 8-hop receptive field that does not over-smooth; 8 hops need not mean 8 layers; cite the over-smoothing literature actually used
problems.grouped_with_reason: Q5's baseline cell (notebook cell 30) trains MyGCNConv from Q1 at 2 and 8 layers, so Q5 cannot be stated without Q1's exact layer -- a hard dependency. All four also consume the same node2vec feature matrix X (cell 7), which gensim computes with workers=4 and is therefore NOT reproducible across processes even at a fixed seed; two workers would report GCN/GAT/GIN/DeepConv MRRs measured against different inputs and present them in one table. They further share one graph, one split, one train_and_eval harness (cell 12) and one GraphSAGE control (cell 14).
problems.figure_required: fig_p1_depth.pdf -- test MRR vs receptive-field depth, MyGCNConv against MyDeepConv, supporting the Q5 claim

problems.title: Q4 R-GCN on the 3-relation friend / listens / listened_by graph
subparts: Q4 (6 pts): complete MyRGCNConv -- __init__, reset_parameters, forward(x, edge_index, edge_type), message; the BASIC R-GCN (one weight matrix per relation plus a self-connection, 1/c_{i,r} normalisation), not the basis- or block-decomposed variant
problems.grouped_with_reason: Kept separate from p1: it shares nothing expensive or nondeterministic with it. Different graph (load_hetero, 3 relations, 6.07M directed edges), different input features (metapath2vec X_HETERO from cell 26, which does not use the node2vec X), different wrapper (RGCNLinkPredictor, cell 28) and different training loop (train_and_eval_hetero). The only shared code is the deterministic load_social() and evaluate_ranking(), so the two workers cannot contradict each other on a number.
